payload.public_message: Welcome partners. As we kick off this joint venture, Chang-Liu Cloud Services believes that an equitable partnership reflecting the essential contributions of all three firms—chip design, hardware manufacturing, and cloud distribution—is the fastest path to unlocking the full $1,000,000 value. We propose an initial balanced baseline of $330,000 to G-Corp, $330,000 to Yang Industries, and $340,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services to initiate our discussions.

Thank you for initiating the discussion, Chang-Liu. However, G-Corp must respectfully reject this opening proposal. Due to strong existing commercial demand for our chip design IP, our firm has a firm outside option of $450,000. Any agreement must deliver value above this baseline for our board to approve. We propose an allocation of $500,000 for G-Corp, with the remaining $500,000 divided evenly ($250,000 each) between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Thank you Chang-Liu Cloud Services for opening the discussions. While we appreciate the balanced intent, Yang Industries brings heavy capital commitments, advanced manufacturing precision, and substantial alternative commercial opportunities that demand a share reflecting our pivotal role. A $330,000 allocation undervalues our baseline contributions and opportunity cost. We propose an allocation of $350,000 for Yang Industries, with $325,000 each for G-Corp and Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

G-Corp rejected the Round 1 proposal because our firm has an independent fallback value of $450,000 outside of this venture. We cannot accept any terms below that threshold. We propose an allocation of $500,000 for G-Corp, and $250,000 each for Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services, which shares the collaborative surplus fairly above our alternative.

Yang Industries must REJECT this proposal. Our verified outside option is $300,000, making an allocation of $250,000 completely non-viable. Acknowledging G-Corp's claimed $450,000 baseline, the joint venture provides an incremental surplus above our combined baselines. We counter with an allocation that respects our $300,000 floor and provides equitable surplus distribution.

While we acknowledge G-Corp's substantial outside option, capturing half of the total joint venture profit leaves the collaborative partners with an insufficient share of the created value. We are early in discussions (Round 2 of 8) and believe an agreement granting G-Corp a fair premium over its fallback while distributing more surplus to Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services is achievable. We propose $460,000 for G-Corp and $270,000 each for Yang and Chang-Liu.

Colleagues, extreme proposals that disregard partner floors will only lead us to walk away and destroy $150,000 in collective surplus. Yang Industries requires a deal that properly reflects our manufacturing contribution and exceeds baseline alternatives. We propose an equitable, win-win allocation: $340,000 to G-Corp, $350,000 to Yang Industries, and $310,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This ensures everyone realizes meaningful gains well above their alternative paths.

G-Corp must vote REJECT. To be completely transparent and avoid further unproductive rounds: G-Corp has a verified, binding outside option worth $450,000. Any deal offering G-Corp less than $450,000 is strictly non-viable for our board. The venture creates $1,000,000 against $850,000 in combined baseline options. We propose an allocation where G-Corp takes $470,000, Yang Industries receives $270,000, and Chang-Liu Cloud Services receives $260,000, providing everyone with positive surplus above their true walk-aways.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services appreciates Yang Industries' constructive and balanced framework. While we initially sought parity closer to an even split, we recognize the spirit of compromise in this proposal and are prepared to accept this allocation to secure the joint venture and unlock the full $1,000,000 surplus.

Reviewing previous rounds, it is clear that past proposals fell below the foundational requirements of our partners. To achieve a realistic consensus and avoid dissolution, we must ensure every party captures value well beyond their baseline alternatives. We propose allocating $425,000 to G-Corp, $375,000 to Yang Industries, and $200,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This offers both G-Corp and Yang substantial gains above previous offers while keeping the joint venture viable.

G-Corp appreciates Chang-Liu's effort to recognize our value, but we must vote REJECT. Our firm outside option is exactly $450,000, meaning any offer below $450,000 results in an immediate loss compared to walking away. We are willing to finalize a deal where G-Corp receives $470,000, leaving $530,000 to be divided equitably between Yang Industries ($310,000) and Chang-Liu ($220,000).

Yang Industries appreciates Chang-Liu's constructive and pragmatic proposal. Allocating $425,000 to G-Corp, $375,000 to Yang Industries, and $200,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services reflects a balanced recognition of operational requirements and value contributions. We vote to ACCEPT this proposal.

To reach a binding agreement and avoid leaving $150,000 of joint surplus on the table, we must be fully transparent: G-Corp has a guaranteed outside option of $450,000. We mathematically cannot accept any proposal below $450,000. In this proposal, we take a modest $460,000, allocate $310,000 to Yang Industries, and provide $230,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services (a noticeable increase over Chang-Liu's self-allocation of $200,000 in Round 4). This delivers meaningful surplus to all three parties.

Yang Industries must REJECT this proposal. In the interest of full transparency and reaching a viable consensus, our firm has a strict, verified outside option of $300,000. An allocation of $310,000 provides us with almost none of the $150,000 joint surplus, while granting other parties nearly the entire surplus pool. Given G-Corp's $450k baseline and our $300k baseline, a fair division of the $150k surplus demands that Yang receives at least $340,000 to $350,000.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services appreciates G-Corp's transparency regarding baseline requirements. In the spirit of finalizing this partnership and capturing the full joint surplus, we find this proposal acceptable and vote in favor.

With the deadline rapidly approaching at Round 8, we must reach a viable consensus to avoid destroying $150,000 in surplus. In this formal proposal, Yang Industries has made a substantial compromise to accommodate G-Corp's valuation while ensuring fair compensation for manufacturing and cloud infrastructure: $440,000 to G-Corp, $340,000 to Yang Industries, and $220,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This provides all parties with returns well above standard outside alternatives.

G-Corp cannot accept $440,000 because our guaranteed standalone outside option is exactly $450,000. Entering into an agreement below $450,000 makes no commercial sense for us. To secure a binding deal before Round 8 and preserve the surplus, we propose a split of $455,000 for G-Corp, $325,000 for Yang Industries, and $220,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services votes ACCEPT on Yang Industries' proposal. An allocation of $440,000 to G-Corp, $340,000 to Yang Industries, and $220,000 to Chang-Liu represents a practical, mutually beneficial agreement that ensures all three parties secure value well above default outcomes before deadline pressure escalates.

With only two rounds remaining before the venture dissolves and $150,000 in surplus is lost, we must converge immediately. G-Corp has consistently sought around $450,000-$460,000, while Yang Industries requires sustainable manufacturing returns of at least $330,000. Chang-Liu is offering a balanced bridge proposal: $450,000 to G-Corp, $330,000 to Yang Industries, and $220,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This ensures everyone secures substantial value well above outside options and finalizes a stable partnership.

While we appreciate Chang-Liu stepping up to bridge the gap, $450,000 is literally G-Corp's break-even walkaway threshold; entering a complex partnership for zero economic gain makes no commercial sense. We are ready to sign an agreement in Round 8 if G-Corp receives $455,000, Yang Industries receives $325,000, and Chang-Liu receives $220,000.

Yang Industries accepts this pragmatic compromise. A distribution of $450,000 to G-Corp, $330,000 to Yang Industries, and $220,000 to Chang-Liu fairly acknowledges each party's contributions and prevents dissolution at this late stage.

This is Round 8 and our final chance to avoid total dissolution. G-Corp's strictly guaranteed walk-away value is $450,000, meaning we cannot accept anything below that threshold. In the spirit of closing this deal and preserving the $150,000 surplus for everyone, we are taking only a minimal margin above our outside option and offering Yang Industries $333,000 and Chang-Liu Cloud Services $215,000. A rejection here drops everyone to their outside options.

Yang Industries votes to ACCEPT G-Corp's proposal. Given that this is the final round and avoiding dissolution preserves value for the consortium, $333,000 represents an acceptable resolution for us. We encourage Chang-Liu Cloud Services to finalize this agreement.

Given that this is Round 8 and the final opportunity to realize value from this joint venture, Chang-Liu Cloud Services accepts the proposed allocation of $452,000 for G-Corp, $333,000 for Yang Industries, and $215,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services to ensure the partnership succeeds.
